title: Mars, Jupiter and Leonid Meteor Shower
excerpt: A lot going on in the coming week, take a look outside in the early morning sky before dawn.
content:
Weather for the past week:

Edgartown Harbor Water temperature: 56°

A lot going on in the coming week, take a look outside in the early morning sky before dawn.

In the wee hours of Monday morning look for the two planets, Jupiter and Mars, side by side, less than two degrees apart. The planets are so close together, close enough to look like they are talking together. You’ll agree, however, Jupiter is 497 million miles away and Mars is much closer at 125 million. The two are closest Monday.

The two have been hanging out together this month  and will continue. But Monday, is the best time because they are so close.

You’ve got another reason to step outside, Tuesday morning, this time for the Leonid Meteor Shower.

You may see as many as a dozen meteors in an hour of viewing. Look up to the constellation Leo, rising in the east. This is where the meteors will appear to originate. The best time is to look in the early morning, though you could see a straggler, an accidental meteor any time in the nights ahead.

M.A.L.
